hints.title: Single Character Equivalence
hints.text: Any equal substring of length > 1 has higher i - j than its single-character prefix; only single characters need evaluation.

hints.title: Smallest i and Largest j
hints.text: For each character a to z, the difference i - j is minimized by picking the earliest occurrence in s1 and latest in s2.

hints.title: Count Minimal Differences
hints.text: Find minimum value of first_index[c] - last_index[c] across all 26 letters, then count how many letters attain this minimum.

hints.title: Full Implementation

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all pairs of indices takes O(n * m) quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Recording first and last letter positions computes minimal difference in O(n + m) time and O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate proves that considering substrings longer than 1 character can never yield a smaller difference.
